name: South Indian Bank Ltd
title: South Indian Bank Ltd - 532218 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Bank posted record FY26 profit of INR1,455 crore (+12%) with GNPA down to 1.43% and Q4 credit cost of 3bp, but management flags credit cost troughed and guides FY27 loan growth of 15-16%.

summary.headline: South Indian Bank FY26 net profit rose 12% to INR1,455 crore; Q4 PAT INR408 crore, GNPA down to 1.43% for the year.
summary.overview: FY26 was the bank's highest-ever annual profit, with deposits up 15% and gross advances up 14.5% (about 15.8% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off). Asset quality improved sharply, with gross NPA at 1.43% and net NPA at 0.29%, and Q4 credit cost was 3 bps. Q4 non-interest income fell mainly because Treasury income was near nil versus about INR77 crore in Q3, and employee costs were lowered by an INR80 crore actuarial write-back. Management said credit cost and slippages are likely to rise from here, and it flagged a CEO succession process, with the current term ending September 30, 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR342 crore in Q4 FY25
Q4 NIM up 9 bps QoQ; Q3 up 6 bps
GNPA down 177 bps from 3.2%; NNPA down 63 bps from 0.92%

financial_highlights.value: 15 bps in Q4 (not annualised); 72 bps for FY26

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book grew 46% in FY26 to INR24,729 crore, average LTV 57.18%, average ticket about INR2.71 lakh. Management said the vast majority is organic; buyouts and co-lending are about 8-10% of the book.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 38% of the loan book; management targets about 33% over time, with ultra-short-duration corporate lending falling from roughly 20-25% of book to about 10%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 15% YoY. Sequential decline of about 2% was attributed to a INR554 crore write-off, per management, with no material stress seen.

segments.name: Retail and mortgage/auto
segments.commentary: Management reported significant YoY growth in mortgage and auto loans. Personal loans are largely pre-approved sales to existing customers, with loss rates of about 3.5-4% against spreads of 11-12%.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury income was nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3, which drove the non-interest income dip. FX revenue grew substantially; a new TF Online export platform is planned.

guidance_outlook: Loan growth guided at 15-16% for FY27, and the bank aims to match industry growth if industry grows faster.
NIM expected to keep widening through asset mix shift to retail and MSME, repricing of about 60-65% of deposits during FY27, and possible rate hikes, where the bank would be a large beneficiary.
Operating expenses will rise as the bank invests in distribution and technology, but management aims for positive operating leverage for a third straight year.
Management expects credit cost and slippages to trend upward from current lows due to Middle East geopolitical stress; it sees Q3 credit cost of 3 bps as the trough.
Branch network to grow selectively in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi; branches fell from 955 to 948 over the past seven to eight quarters.
Corporate share targeted to fall from 38% to about 33% of the loan book over two to three years.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 948, down from 955 over seven to eight quarters; selective additions planned in several states.
SIB RED, a full digital bank offering, launched towards end-March 2026.
New TF Online platform under development for export and trade finance for corporate and MSME clients.
Management said investment in distribution, manpower and technology will start, after costs were held flat for eight to ten quarters.
demand_pricing: Deposit cost rose about 3 bps QoQ in Q4 as the bank selectively repriced deposits to fund growth; management said it had been priced below competitors.
NRI deposits grew 12% in FY26 versus 7% in FY25; management said there is no stress from West Asia conflict, with a slight pickup in inward remittances.
Management said the new ECLGS-type scheme targets airlines and MSMEs, and it did not expect a material drawdown given the current borrower stress levels.
Gold price fell from about $5,500 to about $4,100 per ounce in January-February; margin calls were met promptly and gold loan risk is managed with a 30-day VaR framework and standard-deviation caps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vinod Francis said Treasury income was almost nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3 because of market conditions. Management said the drop was industry-wide and that the shift to retail and MSME should raise fee income over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off in employee expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was an actuarial valuation write-back of close to INR80 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost and ECL transition look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 credit cost of 3 bps is the trough and expects slippages and credit cost to rise given geopolitical stress; it cannot quantify this. For ECL transition, no floating provision is held and no material one-time impact is expected, given SMA 1 and 2 at about 0.6% of the book and PCR near 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the cost of deposits rise, and will NIM keep improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank repriced deposits slightly to support growth, adding about 3 bps. It said NIM rose about 15 bps over two quarters and expects further widening from mix, repricing of 60-65% of deposits, and rate hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO succession on track?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO P.R. Seshadri said the Board is actively searching and will send names to RBI in time. His term ends September 30, and management expects the new incumbent to be in place before or just after that date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank add branches or expand distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will add branches selectively in the under-penetrated states, and rely more on DSAs, digital channels and the SIB RED digital bank.

risks_watch: Rising slippages and credit cost, which management expects from Middle East stress; the outcome is unquantified.
Gold price volatility on a book of INR24,729 crore; a fall beyond the VaR-based caps would hit the bank, and the portfolio's LTV is blended.
Fee income volatility from Treasury; Q4 Treasury income was near nil.
Deposit cost pressure from selective repricing, versus expected repricing benefit in FY27.
CEO succession: the search is ongoing and the term ends September 30, 2026.
Old and new book classification was debated internally; the old book was about 12% of gross advances, and the Q4 GNPA reduction was largely driven by INR1,048 crore of technical write-off.
Possible difficulty recovering the 25% ECLGS guarantee portion if settlements are made with borrowers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and NIM direction, but cautious on credit outlook, where the CEO said he could not quantify the impact. Evasive on the CEO succession timeline and on some data points, which were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: The bank declared its highest ever net profit for the year at INR1,455 crores for the financial year 2025-2026, which implies a growth of 12% compared to INR1,303 crores in the prior year.
I think if anything, both slippages and credit cost should trend upwards, especially given the geopolitical stresses that we see emanating from the Middle East and elsewhere.
So over the last two quarters our NIMs have improved by about 15 basis points, I mean six basis points in Q3 and nine basis points in Q4.

adds.what: Selective branch additions in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi (branch count 948, down from 955 over 7-8 qua

growth.why: Management guides FY27 advances growth of 15-16% (midpoint 15.5%), backed by gold loans (book up 46% to INR24,729 crore), mortgage/auto growth, and NRI deposits (+12%), but no specific capacity or order book is quantified; branch network is shrinking and investment in distribution is only starting.

mgmt.note: CEO succession process flagged; current CEO term ends September 30, 2026, no successor named and no new growth plan stated.
